subsystems.name: Optical sensor module
subsystems.role: shines light through the skin and reads how much comes back, which tracks the pulse.

subsystems.name: Motion and temperature sensors
subsystems.role: separate true physiology from hand movement and track skin temperature overnight.

subsystems.name: Electronics core
subsystems.role: runs the sensors and stores or sends the data.

subsystems.name: Power
subsystems.role: fits a battery into a few cubic centimetres.

subsystems.name: Mechanical body
subsystems.role: holds everything against the finger without pinching it.

subsystems.name: Algorithms and app
subsystems.role: turn raw light and motion signals into sleep, heart-rate and recovery metrics.

buildSteps.title: Fix the optical geometry
buildSteps.detail: The LED-to-photodiode spacing, usually a few millimetres, is chosen so light reaches the artery-rich tissue of the finger rather than bouncing along the surface.

buildSteps.title: Design the ring body
buildSteps.detail: The shell is machined or moulded in sizes spanning roughly 15–23 mm inner diameter, with opaque walls between emitters and detectors to block light piping.

buildSteps.title: Make the flexible circuit
buildSteps.detail: A rigid-flex printed circuit board carrying the LEDs, photodiodes, chip and antenna is formed into a cylinder small enough to fit the band.

buildSteps.title: Assemble power and electronics
buildSteps.detail: A thin curved battery and inductive coil are placed against the board and the assembly is fitted into the shell.

buildSteps.title: Encapsulate and seal
buildSteps.detail: The optics are potted in a clear, skin-safe resin that transmits infrared light and survives daily water and sweat exposure.

buildSteps.title: Calibrate each unit
buildSteps.detail: Because finger size and skin tone change how much light returns, optical output is tuned per unit and per wearer.

buildSteps.title: Train the algorithms
buildSteps.detail: Models are developed by recording ring signals alongside reference measurements such as laboratory sleep studies, ECG and finger-cuff blood pressure.

buildSteps.title: Validate and ship
buildSteps.detail: Performance is tested against reference devices and the device is released with firmware updates over the air.

prerequisites.why: the whole product depends on cheap, tiny LEDs and photodiodes sensitive enough for a finger.
the battery is far too small for anything that draws milliamps continuously.
raw pulse and motion signals are meaningless to users until they become sleep stages and heart-rate variability.
estimates from pulse timing drift with posture, temperature and exercise, so no consumer ring yet offers clinically reliable blood pressure; the tile's claim is aspirational.
some rings have clearance for atrial-fibrillation notification; general diagnostic use is mostly not approved.
measuring glucose or hydration through skin optics has not been shown to work reliably.

pathway.milestone: rings that reliably track sleep, heart rate, heart-rate variability, skin temperature and activity
pathway.unlocks: all-day, all-night monitoring in a form factor people actually keep on.

pathway.milestone: cleared detection of irregular rhythms and better oxygen-saturation accuracy across skin tones
pathway.unlocks: early warning of conditions that currently go unnoticed.

pathway.milestone: cuffless blood pressure with periodic cuff calibration and regulatory clearance
pathway.unlocks: the metric the tile promises, and the one most likely to change clinical care.
continuous monitoring of blood glucose or hydration — still laboratory research.
